Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Framework

The manifesto outlines a "mission-driven government" approach with five central priorities: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, opportunity expansion, and NHS reform. The document establishes fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt as a share of GDP by the fifth forecast year.

## Economic Policy

Labour proposes establishing an Industrial Strategy Council and National Wealth Fund capitalised at £7.3 billion to attract private investment. The plan includes capping corporation tax at 25%, maintaining full expensing for capital investment, and reforming business rates in England. A ten-year infrastructure strategy would guide investment priorities.

The manifesto commits to building 1.5 million homes over the parliament through planning reform, including updating the National Policy Planning Framework, restoring mandatory housing targets, and developing "grey belt" land with community benefit requirements. A new generation of new towns is proposed alongside social housing expansion.

Employment reforms include banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, ending fire-and-rehire practices, establishing basic employment rights from day one, and creating a Single Enforcement Body for workplace rights.

## Energy and Environment

The plan targets zero-carbon electricity by 2030 through doubling onshore wind, tripling solar power, and quadrupling offshore wind. Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland and capitalised at £8.3 billion, would co-invest in clean energy projects.

The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion to upgrade five million homes. The manifesto proposes extending the Energy Profits Levy, removing investment allowances, and closing windfall tax loopholes. No new oil and gas exploration licences would be issued, though existing licences would continue.

Water companies would face enhanced regulation, with powers to block executive bonuses and bring criminal charges for persistent pollution.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include delivering two million additional operations and appointments annually, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and establishing specialist rape units in every police force. The manifesto commits to delivering the NHS long-term workforce plan and reforming the dental contract.

Social care would move toward a National Care Service with national standards, including a Fair Pay Agreement for adult social care workers.

Education proposals include recruiting 6,500 teachers, opening 3,000 primary school nurseries, providing free breakfast clubs in every primary school, and launching a curriculum review. The Conservatives' private school VAT exemption would end to fund state school investment. Further education colleges would become specialist Technical Excellence Colleges, and the apprenticeship levy would be reformed into a Growth and Skills Levy.

## Criminal Justice

A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee would recruit additional officers, PCSOs, and special constables. New Respect Orders would address antisocial behaviour, and a specific offence for assaults on retail workers would be created. Youth intervention measures include Young Futures hubs with mental health support and a new offence of criminal exploitation of children.

The manifesto targets halving violence against women and girls within a decade, including fast-tracking rape cases through specialist courts and placing domestic abuse experts in emergency call centres.

## Immigration and Borders

A Border Security Command would coordinate hundreds of investigators to tackle people smuggling, funded by ending the Rwanda partnership. Additional caseworkers would address asylum backlogs, and a returns unit with 1,000 staff would expedite removals. The document proposes seeking a security agreement with the EU for intelligence sharing.

Labour would reform the points-based immigration system, linking it to skills policy and establishing workforce plans for sectors dependent on overseas workers.

## Constitutional and Governance Reforms

Proposed changes include removing hereditary peers' voting rights, introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for Lords members, and consulting on an alternative second chamber. An Ethics and Integrity Commission would oversee ministerial standards, and a Modernisation Committee would reform Commons procedures.

Devolution would deepen through new Combined Authority powers, Local Growth Plans, and a Council of the Nations and Regions bringing together the Prime Minister with First Ministers and Metro Mayors. Voting age would lower to 16.

## Foreign Policy and Defence

The manifesto commits to NATO membership, the nuclear deterrent, and a Strategic Defence Review within the first year, with a path to spending 2.5% of GDP on defence. AUKUS partnership continues, and Ukraine would receive sustained military and financial support.

EU relations would be reset through a veterinary agreement, mutual recognition of professional qualifications, and a UK-EU security pact, while remaining outside the single market, customs union, and freedom of movement.

The document supports Palestinian statehood recognition and commits to restoring 0.7% GNI development spending when fiscal circumstances allow.
